plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with tiny, fragrant purple flowers. In early July the fields hum with bees and the air carries a sweet, herbal perfume.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, peaking in July
plants.location: Provence, France, and temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its flowers have been used for centuries to scent linens, soaps and perfumes.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. In midsummer prairies and gardens glow with them, and butterflies and goldfinches visit often.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn, peaking in July
plants.location: Central and eastern North America, in prairies and open woodlands
plants.funFact: The central cone is a dense head of many tiny fertile florets. Goldfinches often eat the seeds in late summer.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, cup-shaped blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. In July they open at dawn over warm ponds and wetlands, with a soft fragrance.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, with peak bloom from June to August
plants.location: Southern and eastern Asia, including China, Japan and India
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves repel water and dirt through a microscopic surface texture. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning materials.
